definitions.explanation: The point at which rays of light converge after passing through a lens or reflecting from a mirror. A technical term in optics and photography.

definitions.gloss: focus, central point (of attention or discussion)
definitions.explanation: The main point of attention, discussion, or concern. The most common usage in everyday language.

examples.japanese: カメラの{焦点|しょうてん}を{合|あ}わせる。
レンズの{焦点|しょうてん}{距離|きょり}が{長|なが}いほど{遠|とお}くのものを{大|おお}きく{撮|と}れる。
examples.english: The longer the focal length of the lens, the larger you can photograph distant objects.

examples.japanese: {虫眼鏡|むしめがね}で{太陽|たいよう}の{光|ひかり}を{焦点|しょうてん}に{集|あつ}めると、{紙|かみ}が{燃|も}える。
examples.english: If you focus sunlight to the focal point with a magnifying glass, the paper will burn.

examples.japanese: {議論|ぎろん}の{焦点|しょうてん}がずれている。
{選挙|せんきょ}の{焦点|しょうてん}は{経済|けいざい}{政策|せいさく}に{移|うつ}った。
examples.english: The focus of the election shifted to economic policy.

examples.japanese: {裁判|さいばん}では、{被告|ひこく}の{動機|どうき}が{焦点|しょうてん}となっている。
examples.english: In the trial, the defendant's motive has become the focal point.

notes:
USAGE:
The figurative sense (focus of attention) is far more common in everyday language than the optical sense. The expression {焦点|しょうてん}を{合|あ}わせる works for both senses — literally focusing a lens or figuratively directing attention.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {焦点|しょうてん}を{合|あ}わせる: to focus, to bring into focus
- {焦点|しょうてん}を{当|あ}てる: to focus on, to spotlight
- {焦点|しょうてん}がずれる: to be off focus, to lose focus
- {焦点|しょうてん}{距離|きょり}: focal length
- {議論|ぎろん}の{焦点|しょうてん}: the focus of discussion
